Closes: #7600 # Fix incorrect block status reporting in Access API (issue #7600) ## Summary Addresses [issue #7600](https://github.com/onflow/flow-go/issues/7600) where the Access API incorrectly reports block status for blocks queried by ID. The core problem was that both GRPC and REST APIs used faulty logic that only compared block heights without verifying that the block at that height was actually the finalized block. **Root cause**: An unfinalized block could exist at the same height as a finalized block (in fork scenarios), and the previous logic would incorrectly report it as finalized or sealed. **Solution**: - Extract shared `determineBlockStatus` function that implements the correct finalization check pattern (already used in `backend_network.go`) - Update GRPC backends (`backend_block_details.go`, `backend_block_headers.go`) to use proper finalization verification - Fix REST API (`blocks.go`) to return actual block status instead of hardcoded `BlockStatusUnknown` ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] **Verify finalization logic correctness**: Review the `determineBlockStatus` function to ensure it properly handles the fork scenario described in issue #7600 - [ ] **Test conflicting block scenarios**: Create test cases with unfinalized blocks at the same height as finalized blocks to verify correct status reporting - [ ] **Validate API consistency**: Ensure GRPC and REST APIs return consistent block statuses for the same blocks - [ ] **Check for regressions**: Test existing block retrieval functionality to ensure no breaking changes to normal operation **Recommended test plan**: Query blocks by ID in a test environment with fork scenarios, particularly focusing on unfinalized blocks that exist at heights where different blocks are finalized. --- ### Diagram ```mermaid %%{ init : { "theme" : "default" }}%% graph TB subgraph "Access API" BD["backend_block_details.go
